title: Resolution of a nodal curve over a smooth normal-crossings pair
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $Y$ be a smooth integral finite-type $F$-scheme. Let $T\subset Y$ be a reduced effective Cartier divisor with strict normal crossings. This means that its finitely many irreducible components are smooth and every intersection of $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth of codimension $r$ in $Y$; the empty divisor is allowed. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective flat finitely presented morphism with $X$ integral, with smooth geometrically integral generic fibre, and with nonempty connected one-dimensional geometric fibres having at worst ordinary double points. Assume $f$ is smooth over $Y\setminus T$. Let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor, finite etale over $Y$ and contained in the relative smooth locus. Then there is a proper birational morphism $r:\widetilde X\to X$ with $\widetilde X$ integral and smooth over $F$ such that $(r^{-1}(|D|\cup f^{-1}|T|))_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a strict normal crossings divisor. Birational means that $r$ induces an isomorphism on dense open subschemes. An effective Cartier divisor is locally cut out by one non-zero-divisor. An ordinary double point has completed geometric fibre ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$.

Conventions for the notions used here: smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; integrality [def-pc-integral-scheme]; finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; projectivity [def-kun-projective]; flatness [def-weil-flat-morphism]; finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; geometric integrality, connectedness and reducedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; etaleness [def-weil-etale-morphism]; closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]; reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]; properness [def-weil-proper-morphism].

Only properness of the modification is asserted; it holds because the source's modifications are projective in the projective-bundle sense.
